topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture’s aims and connects cellular cancer genetics to the preceding histopathology practicals.

topics.label: From tumor viruses to cellular oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how research into cancer-causing viruses established that transformation originates in altered normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental assessment of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how laboratory assays test whether genes and mutations confer transformed properties on cells.

topics.label: Cancer-gene classification and mutation-specific function
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects and show why those effects depend on the particular mutation and its cellular context.

topics.label: Genetic instability and defective DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish sequence from chromosomal instability and explain how failures in DNA repair produce these abnormalities.

topics.label: Replication and mitotic errors in tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how errors during genome copying and segregation generate instability that can accelerate tumor adaptation and progression.

topics.label: Inherited cancer predisposition and the fate of inherited defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how inherited cancer-gene defects predispose to malignancy while showing that an established tumor can remain malignant after the original defect is corrected.

topics.label: Questions, further reading and the next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This closing concludes the lecture by inviting questions, recommending reading and previewing the next session.
